examples.solution_text:
The denominators are already the same. Add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator.

(a) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{4x}{9}+\frac{2x}{9}\\&=\frac{4x+2x}{9}\\&=\frac{6x}{9}\\&=\frac{2x}{3}\end{aligned}$

(b) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{7a}{12}-\frac{3a}{12}\\&=\frac{4a}{12}\\&=\frac{a}{3}\end{aligned}$

(c) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{5p}{8}-\frac{3q}{8}\\&=\frac{5p-3q}{8}\end{aligned}$

The terms $5p$ and $3q$ are unlike, so they cannot be collected.

examples.question_text:
Write each as a single simplified fraction.
(a) $\frac{h}{6}+\frac{h}{4}-\frac{h}{3}$
(b) $\frac{t}{5}-\frac{t}{2}$
(c) $3y+\frac{y}{4}$
examples.solution_text:
(a) The lowest common multiple of $6$, $4$ and $3$ is $12$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{h}{6}+\frac{h}{4}-\frac{h}{3}\\&=\frac{2h}{12}+\frac{3h}{12}-\frac{4h}{12}\\&=\frac{h}{12}\end{aligned}$

(b) Use denominator $10$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{t}{5}-\frac{t}{2}\\&=\frac{2t}{10}-\frac{5t}{10}\\&=-\frac{3t}{10}\end{aligned}$

(c) Write the whole term as a fraction with denominator $4$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3y+\frac{y}{4}\\&=\frac{12y}{4}+\frac{y}{4}\\&=\frac{13y}{4}\end{aligned}$

Multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators, then simplify.

(a) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{6r}{7}\times\frac{7s}{9}\\&=\frac{42rs}{63}\\&=\frac{2rs}{3}\end{aligned}$

(b) A pronumeral multiplied by itself becomes a power.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{5x}{6}\times\frac{3x}{10}\\&=\frac{15x^2}{60}\\&=\frac{x^2}{4}\end{aligned}$

Multiply by the reciprocal of the fraction being divided by.

(a) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{7m}{12}\div\frac{14}{9}\\&=\frac{7m}{12}\times\frac{9}{14}\\&=\frac{63m}{168}\\&=\frac{3m}{8}\end{aligned}$

(b) The divisor contains $n$, so $n$ must not be zero.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{5n}{8}\div\frac{15n}{4}\\&=\frac{5n}{8}\times\frac{4}{15n}\\&=\frac{20n}{120n}\\&=\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A tank holds $V$ litres when full. It contains $\frac34$ of a full tank. An amount equal to $\frac25$ of a full tank is used. Write the amount left as a single simplified algebraic fraction.
examples.solution_text:
Both fractions refer to the full tank. Subtract the amount used from the amount present.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{3V}{4}-\frac{2V}{5}\\&=\frac{15V}{20}-\frac{8V}{20}\\&=\frac{7V}{20}\end{aligned}$

The amount left is $\frac{7V}{20}$ litres.

examples.question_text:
Write each as a single simplified fraction.
(a) $\frac{2a}{3}+\frac{b}{4}$
(b) $\frac{q}{3}+\frac{q}{6}-2$
(c) $2\pi-\frac{\pi}{5}$
examples.solution_text:
(a) Use denominator $12$. Unlike terms remain separate in the numerator.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{2a}{3}+\frac{b}{4}\\&=\frac{8a}{12}+\frac{3b}{12}\\&=\frac{8a+3b}{12}\end{aligned}$

(b) Use denominator $6$, including for the whole number.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{q}{3}+\frac{q}{6}-2\\&=\frac{2q}{6}+\frac{q}{6}-\frac{12}{6}\\&=\frac{3q-12}{6}\\&=\frac{q-4}{2}\end{aligned}$

(c) Keep $\pi$ exact and collect its coefficients.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2\pi-\frac{\pi}{5}\\&=\frac{10\pi}{5}-\frac{\pi}{5}\\&=\frac{9\pi}{5}\end{aligned}$

(a) Write the whole number with denominator $1$, then multiply.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{2k}{7}\times14\\&=\frac{2k}{7}\times\frac{14}{1}\\&=\frac{28k}{7}\\&=4k\end{aligned}$

(b) The reciprocal of $14$ is $\frac{1}{14}$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{7w}{8}\div14\\&=\frac{7w}{8}\times\frac{1}{14}\\&=\frac{7w}{112}\\&=\frac{w}{16}\end{aligned}$
